subject: physics
question_text: What is the angle of repose? Write its relation to the coefficient of static friction.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The angle of repose is the smallest angle
of an inclined plane at which a body placed
on it just begins to slide down on its own.
steps.why: It is a way of measuring friction with nothing but a protractor — tilt the plane until the body moves.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the angle at which the body is at rest — it is the angle at which it just STARTS to move.

recall.must_convey: That it is the smallest angle of an incline at which a body just begins to slide down.
accept: angle at which the body just begins to slide

steps.memory_tip: Tilt a plank with a coin on it. The angle at the moment the coin starts to slide is θ.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words "just begins to slide" carry it — an angle of rest is a different claim.

steps.why: Both mg terms cancel, so the angle depends only on the surfaces — the mass of the body never appears.
common_mistakes: Writing sin θ = μ_s instead of tan θ = μ_s.

recall.must_convey: That tan of the angle of repose equals the coefficient of static friction.
accept: tan of the angle equals the coefficient of static friction
reject: angle at which the body just begins to slide

steps.memory_tip: TAN, not sin — it is mg sin θ over mg cos θ, and the mg cancels.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The boxed tan θ = μ_s, plus the line saying the mass never enters.

insider_note: The definition is one mark, tan θ = μ_s is the other. A definition on its own answers only half of what is asked.
